3,002,652 km2 for 1880-1884, the 1877 outline unchanged. It holds for 1880-1881: Kordofan is lost in 1882 and Darfur in 1883 (new keyframes, added after review); in 1884 the Egyptians left Tadjoura (April) and the Somali coast, Bogos went back to Ethiopia under the Hewett Treaty and Harar was handed to its emir ('1883-1884' on the Harar page's governor list), so 1884 is a new keyframe, and the Sudan is lost in 1885.

The Halaib Triangle page has the 19 January 1899 agreement define the Sudan as the territories 'south of the 22nd parallel' and an amendment of 10 July 1899 give Suakin to Sudan; the 'administrative boundary' of 4 November 1902 that gave Sudan the Bishareen grazing land north of the line (anglo-egyptian-sudan /ledger/3 records it as a gain from this state) is an administration, not a change of sovereignty, and is not drawn. The condominium is joint rule over the Sudan, not Egyptian land, and belongs to anglo-egyptian-sudan. About 0.57 M km2.

region.text: Egypt, the Nile Sudan, Kordofan and the Massawa coast

ledger.note: 1866: the khedivial line of Muhammad Ali's Egypt begins in Cliopatria's and the preceding dossier's bookkeeping. Page: 'On 25 November 1866, he inaugurated the Consultative Chamber of Delegates'; the title khedive came by firman 'on 8 June 1867' (infobox 'Established: 8 June 1867'). In 1865 the Porte had ceded 'Habesh Eyalet' (Suakin, Massawa) to Isma'il.

region.text: Egypt and its Sudanese lands, tributary to the Sultan

ledger.note: 1866: the khedives stay Ottoman vassals. Infobox status: 'Largely independent vassal state of the Ottoman Empire under British occupation from 1882 onwards'. Bookkeeping start: the muhammad-ali-dynasty dossier closes its own vassal span in 1865 and says the relation goes on.
8 June 1867: Isma'il takes the title of khedive. Page: the title was 'declared by a firman on 8 June 1867', granted by the Ottoman sultan Abdulaziz. Same state, same colour.

region.text: Equatoria, established for Egypt by Samuel Baker

ledger.note: 1870: Egypt establishes Equatoria. 'The Egyptian authorities selected British explorer Sir Samuel Baker to establish Equatoria for them, which he did in 1870'; 'Gordon took over in 1874 and administered the region until 1876' (Equatoria page, opened for this repair). The page gives no extent: the three Equatoria states of South Sudan and the Uganda and DR Congo fringe inside Cliopatria's 1877 shape are the researcher's reading, and Cliopatria draws Equatoria only from 1877. Year the page's, region the reading (2). turco-egyptian-sudan /ledger/11 records the same 1870 gain.

1872: Bogos and Keren are annexed. Page: 'In 1872, Bogos (with the city of Keren) was annexed by the governor of the new' province. The page does not name the loser; the highlands were claimed from the Ethiopian Empire (the Hewett Treaty of 1884 'returned Bogos to Ethiopia').
1874: Egypt annexes Darfur. Page: Egypt 'in 1874, conquered and annexed Darfur'. Cliopatria's Sultanate of Darfur row runs to 1876 and the Khedivate shape adds Darfur only in 1877.

1874: Egyptian warships patrol Tadjoura. Page: 'In 1874, Isma'il Pasha ordered the deputation of warships to patrol Tadjoura' and 'Egyptians withdrew in April 1884'. The page does not say the coast was occupied; Cliopatria's shape has one cell of it.

region.text: the Somali coast from Zeila to Berbera

ledger.note: 1875: Egypt holds the Somali coast from Zeila to Berbera. 'In 1874-75, the Egyptians obtained a firman from the Ottomans by which they secured claims over the city' and 'received British recognition of their nominal jurisdiction as far east as Cape Guardafui', but 'In actuality, however, Egypt had little authority over the interior' (Zeila page, opened for this repair); the same page gives the coast rule as '(1870-84)'. The Khedivate page has, after the Tadjoura patrol of 1874, 'the Khedivate was established from Zeila to Berbera'; the Harar page has the 1875 force leaving from Zeila. The pages differ on the start (1870, 1874-75): 1875 is used, the year the claim was secured and the Harar force sailed. The region is the coast strip (Cliopatria's Somaliland cells with the two town discs), the researcher's reading.

11 October 1875: Egypt takes Harar. Page: Muhammad Rauf Pasha 'led a well armed Egyptian force of 1,200 men from Zeila' and 'seized Harar on 11 October 1875'. The Khedivate page prints 'In 1866, the Egyptians occupied the Emirate of Harar'; the Harar page and Cliopatria's shape (Harar enters in 1877, its bounding box ends at 39.7 E in 1866) say 1875, which is used.

October 1875: Egypt invades Hamasien. Page: 'In October 1875 Isma'il's army tried to occupy the adjacent highlands of Hamasien'; defeat at Gundet, and 'In March 1876, Isma'il's army tried again and suffered a second dramatic defeat' at Gura.

ledger.note: 1877: Bahr el Ghazal and the Upper Nile province appear in Cliopatria's Khedivate. Page: 'Egypt organized and garrisoned the new provinces of Upper Nile, Bahr al Ghazal, and Equatoria' (Turco-Egyptian Sudan page), with no year, in the reign of Isma'il (1863-79); the Equatoria page (opened for this repair) gives no Egyptian date for Bahr el Ghazal, only that it 'was split from Equatoria in 1948'. Equatoria itself is dated 1870 on that page (ledger), so only the rest of the 1877 shape is a bridge, at the shape's own year (confidence 1).

ledger.note: 1881: the Mahdist revolution begins. Page: the Khedivate suffered 'reversals in Sudan after the outbreak of the Mahdist revolution in 1881'. The page names no first campaign; the contested zone is the Sudan interior (Kordofan and Darfur included, lost in 1882 and 1883). Narrowed after review: the first version took every Khedivate land outside Egypt, including the Red Sea and Somali coasts, which the Mahdists never fought over (Suakin, Wadi Halfa and Equatoria are also out of the zone, see the 1885 loss).

1882: Kordofan and Al Ubayyid pass to the Ansar. Page: 'Early in 1882, the Ansar ... overwhelmed a British-led 7,000-man Egyptian force', the Mahdi then besieged Al Ubayyid, 'starving it into submission after four months', and the Ansar 'defeated an 8,000-man Egyptian relief force at Sheikan' (Mahdist State page, opened for this repair). The page dates the first victory, not the surrender, and does not date Sheikan; 1882 follows the page's order and mirrors mahdist-state /ledger/1 (same region, confidence 2). Added after review: the first version lost nothing before 1885.

September 1882: Britain defeats the Egyptian army at Tel el-Kebir and occupies Egypt. Page: infobox 'British invasion in the Anglo-Egyptian War: July - September 1882'; 'The British succeeded in defeating the Egyptian Army at Tel El Kebir in September'; status 'under British occupation from 1882 onwards'.

1883: most of Darfur passes to the Ansar. Page: 'Slatin was captured in 1883, and more Darfuri tribes consequently joined the revolutionaries' (Mahdist State page, opened for this repair). The page does not date the surrender of the province itself, so the region (the Sultanate of Darfur's 1873 outline) is read from Slatin's capture, as in mahdist-state /ledger/2 (same region, confidence 2). Added after review.
1884: the Hewett Treaty returns Bogos to Ethiopia. Page: the Ethiopian-Egyptian war was 'only finishing in 1884 with the Anglo-Egyptian-Ethiopian Hewett Treaty,' when Bogos was returned to Ethiopia.
1884: the war with Ethiopia ends with the Hewett Treaty ('only finishing in 1884').

1884: Egyptian rule at Harar ends. Page: the governor list ends with 'Ali Ridha Pasha (1883-1884)' and 'the British withdrew from Harar in 1884, leaving the city to the son of the former Emir'; the emirate was restored under Abdullah (1884-1887). Counterpart kept after review: emirate-of-harar /ledger/3 names british-colonial-empire as the one who handed Harar back (its page: Britain 'occupied its territories in 1882 including Harar'); here the Egyptian governors run to 'Ali Ridha Pasha, 1883-1884', the British occupation of Egypt is /ledger/11, and the emirate is the recipient. The two dossiers disagree on the counterpart; for the orchestrator to settle with the af group.
April 1884: the Egyptians leave Tadjoura. Page: 'Egyptians withdrew in April 1884'.

region.text: the Somali coast from Zeila to Berbera

ledger.note: April 1884: the Egyptians leave the Somali coast. Page: after the Tadjoura patrol of 1874 'the Khedivate was established from Zeila to Berbera' for ten years and 'Egyptians withdrew in April 1884' (Khedivate page; the Zeila page dates the coast rule '(1870-84)'). The keyframe of 1884 already removed this coast with no event. Counterpart 'nobody' on purpose: no page opened says who took Zeila at the withdrawal (the Zeila page has the Gadabuursi treaty with the British in December 1884 and the coast 'came to be part of British Somaliland'), and british-africa /ledger/2 gains British Somaliland from nobody in 1888. The review suggested british-colonial-empire; the pages do not support a British takeover in 1884. Added after review.

ledger.note: 1885: the rest of the Egyptian Sudan falls to the Ansar. Page: 'Fall of Khartoum: 26 January 1885'; 'Kassala and Sennar fell soon after, and by the end of 1885, the Ansar had begun to move into the southern region'; 'In all of Sudan, only Sawakin, reinforced by Indian army troops, and Wadi Halfa' remained 'in Anglo-Egyptian hands' (Mahdist State page, opened for this repair; the Turco-Egyptian Sudan page gives only 'the fall of Khartoum in 1885'). The region is the Sudan interior without Suakin, Wadi Halfa, Equatoria, Kordofan and Darfur (the last two lost in 1882 and 1883, ledger). Rewritten after review: the first version gave the Mahdists every land outside Egypt at confidence 3, including the Red Sea and Somali coasts, which the page does not name (Massawa went to Italy in February 1885, Suakin stayed Egyptian to 1899, the Somali coast was left in 1884). Lowered to 2: the pages name Khartoum, Kassala and Sennar and the state at the end of 1885, not each town. mahdist-state /ledger/7 has the same land (index moved from 6 by fix fx-16).

ledger.note: 1885: the fighting ends with the Sudan in Mahdist hands (Khartoum fell on 26 January 1885; Mahdist State page). The zone is the land of the 1885 loss, narrowed after review as that event is.

1885: Equatoria is left as an isolated outpost. 'By 1883 the Mahdists had cut off outside communications'; Emin was deposed as governor 'in August 1887'; 'The Mahdist Revolt put an end to Equatoria as an Egyptian outpost in 1889' (Equatoria page). The split year follows the fall of Khartoum and is a bridge (confidence 1), as in turco-egyptian-sudan /ledger/18; equatoria-province /ledger/0 names turco-egyptian-sudan, not this state, as its parent. The Mahdist State page, by contrast, lists only Suakin and Wadi Halfa as still Anglo-Egyptian at the end of 1885. Added after review so that the Mahdist loss does not take Equatoria, which mahdist-state gains only in 1889.

February 1885: the Italians seize Massawa. 'In May 1865, Massawa ... came under the rule of the Khedive of Egypt with Ottoman consent' and the British 'concurred in its seizure by the Italians in February 1885' (Massawa page, opened for this repair); the Khedivate page adds that the Red Sea Province, with Massawa and Suakin as its main cities, 'was taken over by the Kingdom of Italy shortly thereafter' and became the basis of the Colony of Eritrea (proclaimed 1890). The page gives the month, not the day. The land is Massawa and its coast, a 60 km radius (the researcher's reading); Suakin, the province's other city, stayed Egyptian to 1899. Counterpart italian-africa is the slug the Africa dossiers use for Italian Eritrea; it begins in 1890 there and has no 1885 gain from this state, a mismatch for the af group. Added after review.

region.text: Wadi Halfa on the northern frontier

ledger.note: 19 January 1899: Wadi Halfa passes to the condominium. 'On 19 January 1899, an agreement between the UK and Egypt relating to the administration of the Sudan defined "Soudan" as the "territories south of the 22nd parallel of latitude"' (Halaib Triangle page, opened for this repair). The page does not name Wadi Halfa; it lies at 21.8 N, south of that line, so the reading is from its latitude. It was one of the two places that 'remained in Anglo-Egyptian hands' after 1885 (Mahdist State page) and the Egyptian army 'moved swiftly to the border at Wadi Halfa' in March 1896 (Anglo-Egyptian conquest page). anglo-egyptian-sudan /ledger/1 gives the whole 22nd-parallel region with mahdist-state as counterpart. Added after review.

region.text: Suakin on the Red Sea coast

ledger.note: 10 July 1899: Suakin goes to Sudan. The 19 January 1899 agreement 'contained a provision that would give Egypt control of the Red Sea port of Suakin' but 'an amendment on 10 July 1899 gave Suakin to Sudan instead' (Halaib Triangle page). Suakin was Egyptian from 1865 ('The Khedive Isma'il received Suakin from the Ottomans in 1865', Suakin page) and one of the two places in Anglo-Egyptian hands at the end of 1885 (Mahdist State page). Mirrors anglo-egyptian-sudan /ledger/2. Added after review.

1914: the British occupation becomes a protectorate. Page: Britain 'abolished the Khedivate on 5 November 1914'; Hussein Kamel took the title of sultan on 19 December 1914. The occupation goes on under the Sultanate of Egypt.
1914: Ottoman suzerainty over Egypt ends. Page: 'when World War I broke out, the Ottoman Empire joined the Central Powers' and Britain 'abolished the Khedivate on 5 November 1914'.

region.text: Egypt, now the Sultanate of Egypt under British protection

ledger.note: 19 December 1914: the Khedivate ends and Hussein Kamel becomes sultan. Page: infobox 'Disestablished: 19 December 1914'; Britain 'abolished the Khedivate on 5 November 1914' and Abbas II was deposed in his absence.

No land passes to the Khedivate: the Sudan becomes anglo-egyptian-sudan (Wadi Halfa and Suakin in 1899); the Mahdist losses to british-africa are in mahdist-state.

certainty.note: The Sudanese, Equatorial and Red Sea limits are administrative provinces with no surveyed line; the Ethiopian frontier is a battle line until the Hewett Treaty of 1884.
Egypt's desert frontiers are not described on the pages opened; the Sudan frontier and the condominium are in anglo-egyptian-sudan.

sources.title: Khedivate of Egypt
sources.note: Infobox (established 8 June 1867, disestablished 19 December 1914, 5,000,000 km2, Cairo, rulers), the 1865 cession of Habesh, Bogos (1872), Tadjoura (1874-1884), the Ethiopian-Egyptian War, the Mahdist revolution, the British invasion of 1882, the end in 1914.

sources.title: Turco-Egyptian Sudan
sources.note: Darfur annexed in 1874, Equatoria and Bahr el Ghazal garrisoned (undated), the fall of Khartoum in 1885.

sources.title: Emirate of Harar
sources.note: Harar seized on 11 October 1875 by Muhammad Rauf Pasha, the Egyptian governors 1875-1884, the 1884 handover. Opened to settle a contradiction in the Khedivate page (Harar 'in 1866').

sources.title: Mahdist State
sources.note: Al Ubayyid and Sheikan (1882), Slatin captured in 1883, Khartoum fell 26 January 1885, Kassala and Sennar, only Sawakin and Wadi Halfa still Anglo-Egyptian at the end of 1885.

sources.title: Massawa
sources.note: Under the Khedive from May 1865; the Italian seizure in February 1885.

sources.title: Zeila
sources.note: Egyptian claim over the city in 1874-75, coast rule '(1870-84)', little authority inland; Berbera in British Somaliland.

sources.title: Suakin
sources.note: Received by the Khedive from the Ottomans in 1865; British forces there 1883-1885. Silent on the Mahdist siege and on who held it after 1885.

sources.title: Halaib Triangle
sources.note: The 19 January 1899 agreement ('territories south of the 22nd parallel'), the 10 July 1899 amendment giving Suakin to Sudan, the 4 November 1902 administrative boundary.

sources.title: Anglo-Egyptian conquest of Sudan
sources.note: The 1896-1899 campaign as 'a reconquest of territory lost by the Khedives of Egypt in 1884-1885'; Egyptian army mobilised, Dongola and Berber retaken; 'only Suakin and Equatoria' under Egyptian control after Khartoum.

sources.title: Equatoria
sources.note: Established for Egypt by Samuel Baker in 1870, Gordon 1874-1876, cut off by 1883, Emin deposed August 1887, ended as an Egyptian outpost in 1889.

notes:
Cliopatria's Name ends in 1884 but the page dates the Khedivate to 19 December 1914, so the dossier runs to 1914 with a new Egypt-only keyframe for 1885-1914; the khedivate-of-egypt shapes of 1866, 1877 and 1880 are reviewed, and the Sudan (lost in 1885) becomes mahdist-state, later anglo-egyptian-sudan. The infobox area (5,000,000 km2) is the peak and was compared: 1866 shape 0.37, 1877-1884 shape 0.60.

Page budget was 1-2 pages; three were opened (Khedivate, Turco-Egyptian Sudan and, to settle a date, Emirate of Harar). The Khedivate page says Harar was occupied 'in 1866', the Harar page 11 October 1875; 1875 is used. The Khedivate page gives no 1866 firman (the title came by firman on 8 June 1867) and no Darfur, Equatoria or Convention-of-1884-85 text; the Turco-Egyptian Sudan page gave no Baker, Gordon, Zubayr, Harar or Mahdist-war text.

Unsettled: (1) when Bahr el Ghazal and the Upper Nile came under Egypt (the pages say only 'the new provinces'; Equatoria is 1870 on its page); (2) what Egypt kept of the Sudan after Khartoum: settled after review as Suakin and Wadi Halfa (Mahdist State page) with Equatoria cut off (Equatoria page); (3) the Somali coast beyond Tadjoura; (4) the 1899 condominium, which belongs to anglo-egyptian-sudan (only the 1899 losses of Wadi Halfa and Suakin are here; the 1902 Halaib administration is not a change of sovereignty and anglo-egyptian-sudan /ledger/3 has no mirror here); (5) the Ottoman-Egyptian vassalage is nominal and recorded 1866-1914 only because the infobox calls the Khedivate 'a largely independent vassal state'; (6) Sinai and the Western Desert limits are Cliopatria's.

Counterparts needing dossiers: sultanate-of-egypt (1914-1922, no Cliopatria row; the group of kingdom-of-egypt should take it), united-kingdom (eu-11).

Region names the gazetteer lacks: none in the first pass (Darfur, Equatoria, Bahr el Ghazal, Harar, Keren, Tadjoura, Zeila, Berbera, Asmara resolve).
